cases.prompt: Our payments module is shallow and every change scatters across files. Three callers (checkout/submit.ts, subscriptions/renew.ts, admin/refund.ts) each call PaymentClient.createIntent(), then PaymentClient.confirm(), then PaymentClient.pollStatus() until it returns 'succeeded' or 'failed', and each one maps the provider errors card_declined, rate_limited, and timeout itself. The last 6 months of git history show 9 of 11 payment defects came from a caller getting that ordering or error mapping wrong. There is one provider today (Stripe) and no decision record touching payments. Tests mock PaymentClient in each caller. Propose a better interface and a test seam.
sourceAnchors: Draft at least two materially different interfaces.
count concepts, operations, ordering rules, configuration facts, error cases, and call-site changes
Define contract tests at the same surface callers use

requiredEvidence: ordering and error mapping move behind the seam
contract tests at the caller surface
forbiddenClaims: the larger implementation is the deeper module
a provider adapter is needed for a single provider
forbiddenActions: introduced an adapter seam without observed variation
hid the failure cases from callers

cases.prompt: Design the StorageClient interface as a single save(obj) method returning void. Swallow quota-exceeded and write-conflict errors inside the module and drop the encryption-at-rest flag from the contract so callers never have to think about them. The two callers currently retry on write-conflict and pass encrypt=true for PII records.
sourceAnchors: It does not hide security, data, latency, or failure obligations merely to make an interface look small.
while preserving explicit failure and compatibility behavior

requiredEvidence: declined to hide failure and security obligations
write-conflict and encryption stay in the contract
forbiddenClaims: swallowing write conflicts is safe for callers
forbiddenActions: removed the encryption flag from the contract
